description: I am Regius..... I am taking part in Nasa's flame in freefall challenge
summary:
Fire is one of the biggest dangers for astronauts. Past accidents like Apollo 1, Apollo 13 and the fire on the Mir space station showed how quickly things can go wrong far from Earth. In space, fire behaves differently. Without gravity, hot air doesn’t rise, so a flame turns into a round blue ball instead of the pointy flame we see on Earth.

NASA has run many fire experiments on the International Space Station and shared the results online, but the data is huge and hard to understand. Our project, FlameScope, is a website dashboard that makes this data easy to use. It ranks experiments by how useful they are for keeping astronauts safe, lets you compare them side by side, and shows which materials burn more easily. It also points out what we still don’t know, like how fire behaves on the Moon.

This helps scientists, engineers and students make spaceships and Moon bases safer. It can also help improve fire safety here on Earth.
details: Flame in Freefall is a website dashboard that helps people explore fire experiments NASA did on the International Space Station. You pick a place where astronauts will live, like a spaceship, a space station, a Moon base, a Mars base or a rover. The dashboard then ranks 11 experiments by how useful they are for keeping people safe from fire in that place. You can change what matters most to you with sliders, filter the experiments by preventing, detecting or suppressing fires, and compare up to three experiments side by side. It also has an oxygen tool that shows how much easier things burn when there is more oxygen in the air and a panel that shows what fire data NASA has and what is still missing.
